title: Microsoft removes WSUS server role in Windows Server 2028
content_md: Microsoft will remove the WSUS server role from Windows Server 2028, the next major release of its server operating system. Introduced in 2005 as Software Update Services (SUS), WSUS (Windows Server Update Services) lets IT administrators manage and distribute updates for Microsoft products across corporate networks with many Windows devices. It gives admins centralized control over the updates, rather than having each device download them individually from Microsoft's servers. Microsoft has officially deprecated WSUS in September 2024 , but said that it still plans to maintain functionality and continue publishing updates through the channel. The change affects enterprise environments that rely on WSUS to manage updates delivered to many devices but does not impact home users or those using Microsoft Configuration Manager. In a recently updated support document, Microsoft went even further and confirmed that Windows Server 2028 removes the WSUS server role altogether. "WSUS remains available and supported in earlier Windows Server releases, including Windows Server 2025, for the duration of each release's support lifecycle. You can continue to use WSUS on those releases to manage updates for supported Windows client and Windows Server releases, which includes updates to Windows Server 2028," it said .
